claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in HEA multilayers is controlled by the interaction between severe lattice distortion and short-range order.
The interaction between severe lattice distortion and short-range order governs dislocation mobility.
The interaction between severe lattice distortion and short-range order governs deformation-twin formation.
Changes in dislocation mobility and deformation-twin formation lead to progressive plastic deformation.
The starting material is a nanoscale FCC/BCC multilayer coating in an undeformed state.
The proposed sustained-loading condition is 500 MPa at 300 K.
After 100 hours of sustained loading, plastic strain is predicted to increase by 20% relative to the starting baseline.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to temperatures of 250–350 K and stresses of 400–600 MPa.
Nanoindentation and microcompression with in-situ TEM, combined with atomistic simulations, can evaluate dislocation mobility, twin formation, and plastic strain.
A plastic-strain increase below 10% after 100 hours would falsify the hypothesis.
Simulation models may not fully capture the experimental conditions.

contradictions.description: The initial state is called undeformed, but it is also assigned a nonzero plastic strain of 0.01; without defining this as an offset or reference value, these descriptions are inconsistent.
